account_effect_in_sample: No rule is kept, so the account with the kept rules is the ten alone. In sample 2014-2021, FP costs, 1 R per trade, plain sum of the official one-position chains, weekly R booked at the exit, all 418 calendar weeks counted (my own code): weekly Sharpe 2.51 on FP server weeks (2.53 on UTC Monday-Sunday weeks; 2.537 in the engineers' variant counting only trades entered 2014-2021); 7,752 trades, +1,150.9 R, +2.75 R a week (sd 7.90), 43.8 % losing weeks, worst week -12.5 R. With = without: 2.51 -> 2.51. Information only, deciding nothing: had IDXRS_1000's in-sample main (failed, not kept) been added at 1 R per pair, the Sharpe would read 2.533 instead of 2.512 (+0.8 %; best-weighting bound +0.8 %), i.e. +0.023 R a week at equal weekly swing; its own weekly Sharpe 0.81 against a break-even of 0.48 (correlation 0.19 x 2.51).

caveats: All five fail in sample. My recomputation from the engineers' trade, stress, neighbour, gross and null files (r2/tracks/round4/synthesis/verify_verdicts.py) gives every judged figure to rounding. None was attacked, because Addendum J attacks only in-sample passes. Nothing goes to 2022-2025, and no look is declared.

IDXRS_1000 misses on one bar only, t 2.15 against 2.5 on 518 pairs. It would need +0.098 R per pair at the same dispersion instead of +0.084, about 16 % more. It is still a fail, and the protocol drops it. Its neighbours with t >= 2.5 cannot replace it: that would be selection after seeing the results.

IDXRS_1000's in-sample profit is concentrated: 2020 gives +19.7 of +43.7 R (without 2020, t 1.29 on 442 pairs), and the 10 best of 518 pairs give +30.5 R. 445 of its 518 pairs are us100/us30. Its weekly correlation with ocm4 + noise30 is 0.234, so part of it is the us100 cluster again.

Gross edges against costs, per trade, in sample: IDXRS_1000 +6.1 bp against 1.6 bp; ger40 Xetra +0.66 bp against about 0.96 bp; LETF +0.24 bp against 1.7 bp; FOMC +0.15 bp against about 6 bp (mostly swap); FX weekend -0.19 bp before costs. Only IDXRS_1000 has a gross edge worth the name.

Costs are the lab's frozen FP model: today's spreads in bp with Dukascopy's intraday shape, modelled slippage, and swaps where charged. There are no broker fill statistics. A wider real cost could only deepen the fails.

Information only: even at its in-sample face value, IDXRS_1000 would have raised the ten's weekly Sharpe by under 1 % (2.51 -> 2.53). Breadth from this pool could not approach the user's x4.4 gap, as Addendum J said before the run.

Round 4 logged 55 configurations (12 + 11 + 11 + 10 + 11), losing ones included, each declared in declared.json before its run (file times checked). My recomputations and the account measure simulate nothing and are not trials.

In sample only. I read the engineers' in-sample trade files and the official trades of the ten, with entry_time < 2022-01-01 and exit_time < 2022-01-01 inside each read call. No price frame and no 2022+ row was read. The two exposures the engineers disclosed touch no verdict: LETF saw two DAX rules' 2022-2025 lines in an idx_eu report before its declaration, and FX printed the keys of recalc/summary.json.

The engineers used slightly different conventions for weeks, year attribution and open details, each written in declared.json before the run. None changes a verdict: each of the other four rules fails at least six bars, and IDXRS_1000 fails its t under every reading (2.15 per pair, 2.28 on weekly sums, 2.14 on the money version).

Data gaps, as the engineers reported them: sparse Q4 2013 index data (IDXRS_1000's first trade is 2014-03-07; LETF has 28 trades in 2014); sparse early-2013 us500 (FOMC lost 17 trades); LETF neighbour (6) is partly a data artifact (no us100/us30 quotes after 16:00 New York in 2016-2017).

Files: I wrote only under lab/r2/tracks/round4/synthesis/ and lab/results/r2/round4/synthesis.json. I modified no existing file and ran no git command that changes anything. The validation_hi files git shows as modified belong to other jobs.
summary_for_the_user_fr:
Aucune des 5 nouvelles règles ne passe sur 2014-2021 : rien n'est gardé, aucun test sur 2022-2025.
La plus proche, la paire d'indices US de 10h à 15h55 (New York) : 518 paires, +0,08 R par paire.
Elle échoue sur la solidité statistique : t = 2,15 pour 2,5 exigé (3,1 avant frais).
Et 45 % de son gain vient de la seule année 2020. Elle est abandonnée, comme prévu par le protocole.
Les 4 autres ne gagnent rien de mesurable après frais (facteur de profit 0,75 à 1,03 ; 355 à 2 012 trades) :
week-end des devises, DAX à l'heure de Francfort, cycle de la Fed, fin de séance Nasdaq contre Dow.
Votre robot reste les dix règles actuelles : Sharpe hebdomadaire 2,5 sur 2014-2021, inchangé.
Même gardée, la meilleure aurait ajouté moins de 1 % à ce Sharpe.
Annoncé avant le test : 83 % de chances que rien ne passe ; l'écart ×4,4 avec votre demande ne viendra pas de là.
Tout est mesuré sur les années de recherche ; rien après 2021 n'a été lu.
